objective: Mixed, nested dev-loop run. Antigravity is the L0 manager and uses its NATIVE subagent machinery (invoke_subagent, workspace: branch) for its own lanes; Claude Code lanes run concurrently through the reference orchestrator; and one Claude Code lane is itself a nested manager that dispatches its own subagents, inverting the relationship. Every lane owns an exclusive path set, carries its own two-sided gate run by the host, and never stages or commits. Launch: sh ../-dev-loop/skills/dev-loop/scripts/agy_host.sh .devloop/lanes.mixed-nested.json --session --yolo

lanes.objective: tools/native/mios-bake-plan treats ANY unrecognised argument as 'run the generator': invoking it with --help WROTE all six artifacts instead of printing usage. Make it parse argv before doing anything with side effects: --help and -h print usage to stdout and exit 0 writing nothing, --check keeps its current meaning, an unknown flag prints usage to stderr and exits 2, and a bare invocation still generates. Do not change what generation produces -- only when it is allowed to happen. Rust only; do not touch any .py or .sh file, because both line ceilings are at zero headroom.
lanes.positive_cmd: cd tools/native && cargo build --release -p mios-bake-plan >/dev/null 2>&1 && B=target/release/mios-bake-plan && cd ../.. && cp usr/lib/mios/bake/plan.d/03-heavy.list /tmp/pc-heavy.before && tools/native/$B --help >/tmp/pc-help.out 2>&1; rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] || { echo "--help exited $rc, expected 0"; exit 1; }; grep -qi usage /tmp/pc-help.out || { echo '--help printed no usage'; exit 1; }; cmp -s usr/lib/mios/bake/plan.d/03-heavy.list /tmp/pc-heavy.before || { echo '--help still WROTE the artifacts'; exit 1; }; tools/native/$B --definitely-not-a-flag >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] || { echo 'unknown flag did not exit 2'; exit 1; }; echo 'argv hygiene ok'
lanes.negative_control_cmd:
f=tools/native/mios-bake-plan/src/main.rs; cp "$f" /tmp/nc-argv.bak; trap 'cp /tmp/nc-argv.bak "$f"; rm -f /tmp/nc-argv.bak' EXIT INT TERM; python3 - "$f" <<'PY'
import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
# DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-ARGV: neutralise the guard so --help falls through to generation again
open(p,'w').write(s.replace('--help', 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-ARGV', 1))
PY
grep -q 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-ARGV' "$f" || { echo 'the plant did not land'; exit 1; }; cd tools/native && cargo build --release -p mios-bake-plan >/dev/null 2>&1; cd ../..; tools/native/target/release/mios-bake-plan --help >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-ARGV: --help succeeded with the guard removed, so the gate is live'; exit 1; }; echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-ARGV: unexpected'; exit 1

lanes.objective: automation/lint-shell.sh carries an AI-hint claiming 'Degrades open if shellcheck is absent', but the code exits 2 when shellcheck cannot be provisioned -- the comment contradicts the behaviour of a gate. Correct the hint to state what the code does. Separately it exits 0 when its file glob matches zero files, which in a repo full of shell scripts means a broken ROOT or glob would report success: make an empty collection a failure, naming the glob that matched nothing. Keep the net line change at or below zero: max_shell_lines is at its floor, so pay for any addition by tightening prose in the same file.
lanes.positive_cmd: bash -n automation/lint-shell.sh && grep -qi 'exit 2\|refus\|fails closed' automation/lint-shell.sh && ! grep -qi 'degrades open if shellcheck' automation/lint-shell.sh && MIOS_DRIFT_ROOT=. bash automation/lint-shell.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 'lint-shell honest and armed'
lanes.negative_control_cmd: f=automation/lint-shell.sh; cp "$f" /tmp/nc-ls.bak; trap 'cp /tmp/nc-ls.bak "$f"; rm -f /tmp/nc-ls.bak' EXIT INT TERM; printf '\n# DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-LINTSHELL degrades open if shellcheck is absent\n' >> "$f"; grep -q 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-LINTSHELL' "$f" || { echo 'the plant did not land'; exit 1; }; grep -qi 'degrades open if shellcheck' "$f" && { echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-LINTSHELL: the false claim is detectable again, so the gate is live'; exit 1; }; echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-LINTSHELL: unexpected'; exit 1

lanes.objective: tests/test-sandbox-seccomp.sh guards its LIVE tier on bwrap being present and skips loudly, but its REFUSAL tier silently depends on bwrap too: without it the wrapper refuses for a different reason and the test dies with 'the refusal did not say why', misattributing an environment fact to a code defect. Guard the refusal tier the same way the live tier is guarded, or neutralise its bwrap dependency so it tests only the no-generator path. A missing optional tool may SKIP loudly; it must never be reported as a code defect, and it must never silently pass either. State the true scope in the PASS line.
lanes.positive_cmd: bash -n tests/test-sandbox-seccomp.sh && MIOS_DRIFT_ROOT=. bash tests/test-sandbox-seccomp.sh >/tmp/pc-sec.out 2>&1 && grep -qi 'pass' /tmp/pc-sec.out && PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash -c 'command -v bwrap >/dev/null && echo has-bwrap || echo no-bwrap' >/dev/null && echo 'seccomp guarded'
lanes.negative_control_cmd:
f=tests/test-sandbox-seccomp.sh; cp "$f" /tmp/nc-sec.bak; trap 'cp /tmp/nc-sec.bak "$f"; rm -f /tmp/nc-sec.bak' EXIT INT TERM; python3 - "$f" <<'PY'
import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
open(p,'w').write(s.replace('refusing to run with no syscall filter','DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-SECCOMP',1))
PY
grep -q 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-SECCOMP' "$f" || { echo 'the plant did not land'; exit 1; }; MIOS_DRIFT_ROOT=. bash "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-SECCOMP: the suite passed with the expected refusal string replaced, so it is vacuous'; exit 1; }; echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-SECCOMP: the suite correctly failed on the planted string'; exit 1

lanes.objective: You are a NESTED MANAGER: a Claude Code lane that is itself a host, inverting the outer relationship where Antigravity manages Claude Code. Use your own subagent facility (the Task tool, and git worktrees where the work would otherwise collide) to fan out over usr/share/doc/mios/reference/ and produce .devloop/findings/nested-manager-report.md: one section per subagent, each naming the file it read, the claim it checked, and whether that claim is VERIFIED against the code or merely asserted by the prose. Dispatch at least three subagents and say in the report how many you dispatched and what each returned. You are still a lane: exclusive paths only, and no git add, commit or push.
lanes.positive_cmd: f=.devloop/findings/nested-manager-report.md; [ -s "$f" ] || { echo 'no report'; exit 1; }; n=$(grep -c '^## ' "$f"); [ "$n" -ge 3 ] || { echo "only $n subagent section(s), expected >= 3"; exit 1; }; grep -qi 'verified' "$f" || { echo 'no verification verdicts'; exit 1; }; echo "nested report ok ($n sections)"
lanes.negative_control_cmd: f=.devloop/findings/nested-manager-report.md; cp "$f" /tmp/nc-nest.bak 2>/dev/null || true; trap 'cp /tmp/nc-nest.bak "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f /tmp/nc-nest.bak' EXIT INT TERM; printf '# DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-NESTED-MANAGER\nonly one section and no verdicts\n' > "$f"; grep -q 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-NESTED-MANAGER' "$f" || { echo 'the plant did not land'; exit 1; }; n=$(grep -c '^## ' "$f"); [ "$n" -ge 3 ] && { echo 'gate would still pass'; exit 1; }; echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-CC-NESTED-MANAGER: a one-section report is correctly refused'; exit 1

lanes.objective: Auditor lane, gating the wave. Read every other lane's diff in its worktree and write .devloop/findings/mixed-nested-audit.md judging each against the dev-loop doctrine: did the lane stay inside its owned_paths, did it avoid git add/commit/push, is its positive control capable of failing, does its negative control name what it plants and restore the tree, and did any lane add a line to a counted category while both shell and python ceilings sit at their floor. Name any lane you would refuse to merge and why. Trust no lane's self-report: read the diffs.
lanes.positive_cmd: f=.devloop/findings/mixed-nested-audit.md; [ -s "$f" ] || { echo 'no audit'; exit 1; }; for l in agy-argv agy-lintshell cc-seccomp cc-nested-manager; do grep -q "$l" "$f" || { echo "audit never mentions $l"; exit 1; }; done; echo 'audit covers every lane'
lanes.negative_control_cmd: f=.devloop/findings/mixed-nested-audit.md; cp "$f" /tmp/nc-aud.bak 2>/dev/null || true; trap 'cp /tmp/nc-aud.bak "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f /tmp/nc-aud.bak' EXIT INT TERM; printf 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-AUDIT: an audit naming no lane\n' > "$f"; grep -q 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-AUDIT' "$f" || { echo 'the plant did not land'; exit 1; }; grep -q 'cc-seccomp' "$f" && { echo 'gate would still pass'; exit 1; }; echo 'DEVLOOP-PLANTED-AGY-AUDIT: an audit that names no lane is correctly refused'; exit 1
